name: Tarka Daal Chawal with Kachumber & Achar
recipeSteps: Boil moong and masoor lentils with turmeric, salt, and water until soft and creamy.
Heat desi ghee in a pan, add sliced garlic, cumin seeds, and whole dried red chillies until golden and sizzling.
Pour hot tarka over the bubbling daal and cover immediately.
Serve hot over steamed Basmati rice with fresh kachumber salad and tangy achar.
chefTip: A squeeze of fresh lemon juice over the daal chawal elevates the earthy lentil flavors.

name: Kadhi Chawal with Pakora
recipeSteps: Whisk besan and sour yogurt with water, turmeric, and salt; simmer on medium flame for 40 minutes stirring continuously until thick and tangy.
Make a batter of besan, sliced onions, potatoes, crushed coriander, and spices, then deep-fry into crispy pakoras.
Drop the hot pakoras directly into the simmering kadhi.
Temper with cumin seeds, curry leaves, and round red chillies in hot oil, and serve over steamed Basmati rice.
chefTip: Use slightly sour (khatta) yogurt to give the kadhi its signature authentic tangy punch.

name: Dahi Phulki with Warm Roti
recipeSteps: Whisk besan with a pinch of baking soda, salt, and water, then drop small spoonfuls into hot oil to make light phulkis.
Soak the fried phulkis in warm water for 5 minutes, gently squeeze out excess water.
Whisk fresh creamy yogurt with roasted ground cumin, black salt, and green chutney.
Immerse soft phulkis in the spiced yogurt, sprinkle chaat masala and red chilli flakes, and enjoy with soft phulkay (roti).
chefTip: Squeezing the phulkis in warm water makes them incredibly soft and allows them to absorb the yogurt completely.

name: Bhindi Masala Fry
recipeSteps: Wash and completely dry okra with a kitchen towel before slicing into rounds.
Shallow fry okra in hot oil until tender and crisp, then set aside.
In the remaining oil, sauté lots of sliced onions until soft, add diced tomatoes, cumin, and spices.
Fold in the fried okra, cover on low flame (dum) for 5 minutes with green chillies, and serve with hot chapati.
chefTip: Never cover the pan during the initial frying of bhindi to ensure zero slime.

name: Aloo Gobi Masala
recipeSteps: Cut cauliflower into florets and potatoes into cubes.
Sauté onions with ginger-garlic paste, cumin seeds, and turmeric until aromatic.
Add potatoes and cauliflower florets with tomatoes and ground spices.
Cover and simmer on low heat in its own steam until potatoes and gobi are fork-tender, then garnish with ginger and cilantro.
chefTip: Do not add excess water; cooking gobi on slow dum makes it flavorful and prevents it from turning mushy.

name: Aloo Matar Salan with Roti
recipeSteps: Sauté onion paste in oil until golden, then add ginger-garlic and tomato puree.
Bhunify with turmeric, red chilli, and coriander powder until oil surfaces.
Add cubed potatoes and tender green peas with 2 cups of water.
Simmer until potatoes and peas are cooked through and gravy is comforting shorba, finished with garam masala.
chefTip: Fresh seasonal peas give a natural sweetness that balances the spices perfectly.

name: Mix Sabzi (Aloo, Gajar, Matar, Methi)
recipeSteps: Dice potatoes and carrots evenly, and shell fresh peas.
Sauté onions with cumin, ginger, and green chillies, then add chopped tomatoes and dry spices.
Add all vegetables and sauté on medium heat for 5 minutes.
Cover tightly on low flame (dum) with fresh methi leaves until vegetables are tender, and serve with paratha or roti.
chefTip: Fresh methi added at the end imparts the signature winter aroma of dhaba-style mix sabzi.

name: Baingan ka Bharta (Smoky Roasted Eggplant)
recipeSteps: Slit eggplants, insert garlic cloves into the slits, and roast directly on an open stove flame until skin is charred.
Peel charred skin, remove stems, and thoroughly mash the smoky flesh.
In a pan, sauté onions, chopped green chillies, and tomatoes in mustard oil until soft.
Mix in the smoky mashed eggplant, simmer for 5 minutes, and garnish with fresh coriander.
chefTip: Inserting garlic inside the eggplant before flame-roasting infuses sweet smoky roasted garlic flavor into the flesh.

name: Palak Aloo (Spinach Potato Curry)
recipeSteps: Wash, chop, and blanch fresh spinach, then coarsely blend or finely chop.
Fry cubed potatoes in a little oil until lightly golden and set aside.
Sauté onions and garlic in ghee, add tomatoes and ground spices.
Combine spinach puree and fried potatoes, cover and simmer until potatoes are fully cooked.
chefTip: Blanch spinach in boiling water with a pinch of sugar for 2 minutes, then plunge into ice water to keep it bright green.

name: Karela Pyaz Fry
recipeSteps: Scrape and slice karela into thin rounds, rub with salt and let sit for 30 minutes, then squeeze out bitter juices.
Deep-fry or pan-fry karela slices until crispy and golden.
In another pan, sauté double the quantity of sliced onions with saunf, kalonji, tomatoes, and dry spices.
Toss in the crispy fried karela with amchur powder and steam on low heat (dum) for 10 minutes.
chefTip: Generous sweet caramelized onions and tangy amchur naturally balance the bitter notes of karela.

name: Chana Pulao with Mint Raita
recipeSteps: Brown sliced onions in oil with bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, and cumin seeds.
Add ginger-garlic paste, slit green chillies, and boiled chickpeas; sauté for 3 minutes.
Add water, bring to a rolling boil, and gently slide in soaked Basmati rice.
Cook until water level recedes, then cover tightly on dum for 15 minutes. Serve with cool mint yogurt raita.
chefTip: Using the chickpea cooking water (aquafaba) to boil the rice gives the pulao deep savory umami flavor.

name: Matar Pulao with Kachumber Salad
recipeSteps: Lightly caramelize sliced onions in ghee with whole cumin, black cardamom, and cinnamon.
Stir in fresh green peas and ginger paste, sautéing for 2 minutes.
Pour in water, season with salt, and add drained basmati rice.
Simmer until holes form on the surface of rice, seal with a lid for 12 minutes on low heat, and fluff with a fork.
chefTip: Do not over-fry the green peas before boiling so they retain their bright green color and plump sweetness.

name: Tahiri (Aloo Pulao / Yellow Spiced Rice)
recipeSteps: Sauté sliced onions in oil with cumin seeds and whole cloves until translucent.
Add diced tomatoes, turmeric, red chilli, and ginger paste; cook until oil releases.
Add cubed potatoes and sauté for 3 minutes, then add water and soaked rice.
Cook until moisture is absorbed, scatter fresh mint and whole green chillies, and dum for 15 minutes.
chefTip: A generous pinch of turmeric gives Tahiri its iconic vibrant golden hue and earthy aroma.

name: Moong Daal Khichdi with Dahi & Papad
recipeSteps: Wash equal parts split moong daal and basmati rice together and soak for 15 minutes.
In a pot, crackle cumin seeds and whole black peppercorns in golden desi ghee.
Add daal, rice, turmeric, salt, and 4 cups of water for a soft comforting texture.
Cook on medium-low until creamy and porridge-like; drizzle hot desi ghee on top and serve with chilled dahi and papad.
chefTip: Khichdi is the ultimate light, soothing Pakistani comfort meal for digestion and relaxed evenings.

name: Dhaba Style Chana Daal Tarka
recipeSteps: Soak chana daal for 1 hour, then boil with salt and turmeric until tender but holding its shape (khilwan).
In a pan, cook a rich masala of chopped onions, ginger-garlic, tomatoes, and coriander powder.
Mix in the cooked daal with a splash of lentil broth, simmer for 5 minutes.
Prepare tarka in hot desi ghee with garlic slices, whole cumin, and dried red chillies; pour sizzling over the daal.
chefTip: Do not overcook chana daal into paste; each lentil grain should be soft yet separate.

name: Bhuni Daal Mash with Green Chillies
recipeSteps: Soak washed daal mash for 2 hours, then boil until 90% tender with firm bite; drain thoroughly.
In hot ghee, fry sliced onions, ginger-garlic, tomatoes, and ground spices until aromatic masala forms.
Gently fold in the drained daal mash without breaking the grains.
Cover on very low heat (dum) for 8 minutes with plenty of ginger juliennes, green chillies, and garam masala.
chefTip: Never stir daal mash vigorously with a sharp spoon; fold gently with a flat spatula to keep grains intact.

name: Daal Palak (Lentils with Fresh Spinach)
recipeSteps: Boil mixed lentils with salt, turmeric, and water until soft.
Add washed chopped spinach into the lentils and cook for 7 minutes until spinach softens and blends with daal.
Heat desi ghee in a ladle, sizzle crushed garlic cloves and cumin seeds until aromatic.
Pour tarka over daal palak and serve hot with chapati or steamed rice.
chefTip: Cooking the spinach directly in the boiling daal preserves all nutrients and gives rich creamy flavor.

name: Classic Aloo Gosht Shorba
recipeSteps: Sauté whole aromatics and meat in oil with ginger-garlic until meat turns golden.
Add fried onion paste and whisked yogurt, bhunify until oil separates from the masala.
Add warm water and pressure cook or simmer until meat is mostly tender.
Add large potato halves, cook until potatoes are tender and broth forms a rich fragrant shorba.
chefTip: Leaving potatoes in large halves lets them soak up the savory bone broth without disintegrating.

name: Aloo Chicken Shorba with Roti
recipeSteps: Brown onions in oil, blend with tomatoes to create smooth gravy base.
Sear chicken with ginger-garlic and spices until sealed and fragrant.
Drop in potato cubes and sauté with chicken for 4 minutes.
Pour in 2.5 cups water, cover and simmer on medium flame until chicken and potatoes are tender.
chefTip: Sprinkle freshly ground garam masala right before serving for that signature homestyle aroma.

name: Anda Curry (Homestyle Egg Salan)
recipeSteps: Prick hard-boiled eggs with a fork, rub with turmeric and shallow-fry until golden blistered exterior forms.
In the same oil, cook onion paste, ginger-garlic, and tomato puree until thick and oil surfaces.
Add water to create a smooth medium gravy, drop in fried eggs and simmer for 5 minutes.
Garnish with green chillies and fresh cilantro; serve with warm roti.
chefTip: Lightly frying the boiled eggs in turmeric oil gives them a delightfully savory skin.

name: Lobia ka Salan (Red Kidney Beans Curry)
recipeSteps: Soak red lobia overnight, then boil with a pinch of salt until melt-in-mouth tender.
Sauté onions until golden, add ginger-garlic and tomato puree with ground spices.
Bhunify masala, add boiled lobia with its rich cooking water, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Mash a few beans against the side of the pot to thicken gravy, serve over steamed rice or with roti.
chefTip: Mashing a small ladle of beans naturally thickens the salan without adding flour or cream.

name: Tori ki Sabzi (Ridge Gourd Salan)
recipeSteps: Peel ridged skin of tori, wash and cut into rounds.
Sauté onions with cumin seeds and green chillies until soft.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, and sliced tori; stir for 2 minutes.
Cover on low flame; tori will release its own natural sweet juices. Cook until tender and serve with roti.
chefTip: Do not add any water; tori cooks wonderfully in its own natural juices.

name: Lauki Chana Daal (Bottle Gourd with Lentils)
recipeSteps: Soak chana daal and peel and cube fresh bottle gourd.
Sauté onions with ginger-garlic and tomatoes until aromatic.
Add chana daal, lauki cubes, and 2 cups water; cook until daal and lauki are both tender.
Temper with sizzling cumin seeds and garlic in ghee; serve warm with chapati.
chefTip: Lauki cooked with chana daal is a sunnah food that is cooling, light, and extremely nourishing.

name: Shami Kabab with Daal Chawal & Salad
ingredients: Shami Kabab Patties (Beef or Chicken with Chana Daal)
recipeSteps: Dip shaped shami kabab patties in lightly whisked egg.
Shallow-fry on a medium-hot tawa with oil until crispy golden-brown on both sides.
Drain on paper towel.
Serve alongside hot Daal Chawal or warm roti with mint raita and sliced onion salad.
chefTip: Egg coating ensures the exterior gets crispy while the spiced meat and lentil interior stays moist.

name: Moong Masoor Daal Tarka with Paratha
recipeSteps: Wash and boil moong and masoor lentils with turmeric, red chilli, and salt until velvety smooth.
Heat desi ghee in a small fry pan, add sliced garlic, curry leaves, and cumin until fragrant.
Pour sizzling tarka into the daal, cover immediately for 2 minutes to trap the aroma.
Serve with warm whole wheat parathas or crisp tawa roti.
chefTip: Using a mix of moong and masoor gives both silky body (from masoor) and rich nuttiness (from moong).

name: Chicken Peshawari Shinwari Karahi
recipeSteps: Sear Chicken in hot ghee with ginger-garlic paste until lightly browned.
Add halved tomatoes and steam covered until skins peel off easily.
Bhunify on high heat with crushed spices until oil surfaces.
Garnish generously with ginger juliennes and fresh green chillies.
chefTip: No onions; pure tomatoes, garlic and crushed black pepper create the magic.

recipeSteps: Sear Chicken in hot ghee with ginger-garlic paste until lightly browned.

Bhunify on high heat with crushed spices until oil surfaces.

chefTip: Use pure desi ghee and cook on high heat until the oil separates.

name: Chicken Sindhi Spicy Biryani with Aloo & Prunes
recipeSteps: Marinate Chicken with yogurt, crushed ginger-garlic, fried onions, and whole spices.
Cook meat into a fragrant rich gravy until tender.
Parboil long-grain aged basmati rice to 75% doneness with whole spices.
Layer rice over meat gravy, drizzle kewra saffron milk, and steam on low dum for 20 minutes.
chefTip: Dried plums (Aloo Bukhara) provide the iconic sour-spicy balance.

name: Daal Roti (Homestyle Moong Masoor Daal with Phulka Roti)
recipeSteps: Boil washed moong and masoor daal with water, turmeric, and salt until tender and creamy.
Knead wheat flour with warm water into soft dough, roll into thin phulkas and puff on open flame.
Prepare sizzling tarka with desi ghee, sliced garlic, cumin seeds, and green chillies; pour over daal.
Serve hot daal with steaming soft phulka rotis, fresh kachumber salad, and a dollop of butter.
chefTip: Rub a touch of desi ghee over the hot puffed phulka rotis for classic Ghar Ka Khana comfort.

name: Sabzi Roti (Bhindi Masala Fry with Phulka Roti)
recipeSteps: Wash and thoroughly dry okra before slicing into rounds to prevent stickiness.
Shallow fry bhindi until lightly crisp; set aside.
SautÃ© onions with cumin seeds, tomatoes, and everyday spices until a rich bhuna masala forms.
Combine fried bhindi into the masala, steam on low dum for 5 minutes, and serve with hot phulka roti.
chefTip: Never cover the pan while frying okra initiallyâ€”this eliminates slime completely.

name: Sabzi Roti (Aloo Gobi Masala with Tawa Roti)
recipeSteps: Cut cauliflower into florets and potatoes into bite-sized cubes.
Heat oil in a handi, sautÃ© finely chopped onions and ginger-garlic paste until golden.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, red chilli, and salt; cook until oil separates.
Add gobi and aloo, cover tightly and cook on gentle flame in their own steam until fork tender.
Sprinkle crushed kasuri methi and fresh coriander, and serve with warm tawa rotis.
chefTip: Do not add excess water; cooking gobi in its own steam keeps the florets whole and deeply flavorful.

name: Sabzi Roti (Homestyle Mix Sabzi with Warm Roti)
recipeSteps: Chop fresh winter vegetables into uniform cubes and wash fresh methi leaves thoroughly.
SautÃ© cumin seeds and green chillies in oil, then add diced tomatoes and ground spices.
Toss in potatoes, carrots, peas, and methi leaves. Cook covered on low heat until tender.
Finish with a spoonful of desi ghee and serve hot with fresh whole wheat rotis.
chefTip: Fresh fenugreek (methi) gives winter mix sabzi its unforgettable fragrant earthy aroma.

name: Daal Roti (Dhaba Chana Daal Tarka with Roti)
recipeSteps: Soak chana daal for 30 minutes, then boil with turmeric and salt until soft yet retaining its shape.
In a wok, fry onions, ginger, and tomatoes into a rich spicy gravy; stir in the boiled daal.
Prepare a sizzling desi ghee tarka with crushed garlic and button red chillies, pour on top.
Serve piping hot with fresh tawa rotis and onion salad.
chefTip: Chana daal should be khari khari (tender but holding distinct shape), never mushy.

name: Crispy Zinger Burger with Masala Fries
recipeSteps: Marinate chicken fillets in seasoned buttermilk with paprika, garlic powder, and white pepper.
Dredge fillets generously in seasoned flour, dip in ice water, and flour again for crunchy flakes.
Deep fry in hot oil until golden crisp and cooked through.
Toast sesame buns, spread chilli garlic mayo, add shredded lettuce, and assemble with crispy chicken.
Serve with piping hot crispy fries tossed in zesty chaat masala.
chefTip: Double dredging and dipping in ice-cold water creates signature crispy flakes on the chicken.

name: Chicken Tikka Pizza with Garlic Mayo Dip
recipeSteps: Roll pizza dough onto a baking pan and dock with a fork.
Spread seasoned pizza sauce, layer with grated mozzarella cheese, smoky tikka chunks, and crisp vegetables.
Bake in a preheated oven at 230C for 12-15 minutes until cheese is bubbly and golden.
Slice into wedges and serve hot with creamy garlic mayo dip.
chefTip: Bake on the lowest oven rack for the first 8 minutes to get a crispy pizzeria-style crust.

name: Chicken Tikka BBQ with Paratha & Mint Chutney
recipeSteps: Make deep gashes in chicken leg quarters and marinate in yogurt, lemon, ginger-garlic, and tikka spices for 2 hours.
Skewer chicken and grill over glowing red charcoal embers, basting with butter until char marks develop.
Give coal dum (smoke infusion) for that authentic Karachi dhaba BBQ aroma.
Serve hot with crispy parathas, sliced onion rings, and tangy mint raita.
chefTip: Basting with melted butter or oil during the last 5 minutes of grilling keeps the chicken tender and juicy.

name: Beef Seekh Kabab BBQ with Naan & Raita
recipeSteps: Mix minced beef with fat, crushed spices, papaya paste, and finely chopped aromatics; knead until sticky.
Mold onto wide flat metal skewers with wet hands into even cylinders.
Grill over glowing coals, rotating frequently until browned and succulent.
Slide gently off skewers and serve immediately with hot sesame naan and mint raita.
chefTip: 20% animal fat in the mince is essential for seekh kababs to stay juicy and avoid drying out.

name: Crispy Quarter Chicken Broast with Dinner Roll & Garlic Sauce
recipeSteps: Brine quarter chicken in saltwater and vinegar for 2 hours for tender juicy meat.
Dip in egg wash, coat thoroughly in seasoned flour blend, shaking off excess.
Deep fry in hot oil until deeply golden and extra crunchy on the outside.
Serve steaming hot with fluffy sweet dinner rolls, crinkle fries, and pungent garlic sauce.
chefTip: Brining chicken before frying is the secret why Pakistani broast stays exceptionally juicy inside.
